question: A person borrows Rs. 20000 at the rate of 6 percent per annum on simple interest for 3 years. He immediately lends it to another person at the rate of 8.5 percent per annum on simple interest for 3 years. What is the value of gain per year?
solution:
Given:

A person borrows Rs. 20000 for 3 years at 6% per annum Simple Interest.

He immediately lends it to another person at 8.5% per annum for 3 years.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate and T = Time 

Calculation:

P = Rs. 20000 and time = 3 years

First rate = 6% and Second rate = 8.5%

As we know,

SI = Prt/100

⇒ [20000 × (8.5 - 6) × 1]/100

⇒ [20000 × 2.5 × 1]/100

⇒ 500

∴ His gain in the transaction per year is 500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Difference of rate for 1 years = 8.5% - 6% = 2.5%

The gain in the transaction for 1 year = 20000 × 2.5/100 = 500
